description: The Niagara-on-the-Lake Rotary Holiday House Tour NOTL has been a beloved tradition and has raised more than $1,500,000 for local and international charitable projects. Each year, our volunteers and our community partners come together to showcase beautiful hi
headings:
Join us for the 27th annual
Niagara-on-the-Lake Holiday House Tour!

Welcome to the 2026 Rotary Holiday House Tour. It is a pleasure to share this much-loved Niagara-on-the-Lake tradition with you as we celebrate our 27th year. 
 
Since the tour began in 1999, generations of guests have returned with family and friends to enjoy the beauty of our town in the holiday season while helping Rotary support important local, international, and youth projects. 
 
This year, we are especially proud to honour two Silver Medallion Homes, first featured on the tour in 2001, 25 years ago. Their return is a wonderful reminder of the people, homes, and loyal patrons who have made this event so special. 
 
On behalf of our Rotary Club, thank you to our generous homeowners, decorators, sponsors, committee members, volunteers, and to each of you for being part of this tradition. We hope you enjoy the tour, feel the warmth of the season, and leave inspired by the good your support makes possible.
 
Jeannie Manning and Cindy Grant
Co-Presidents 2026-2027

title: NORTHERN BC
description: NORTHERN BCTourism associationThe Northern BC Tourism Association (NBCTA) is dedicated to developing, supporting, and sustaining the tourism sector across northern British Columbia, a region defined by its iconic The Gre
headings: The Northern BC Tourism Association (NBCTA) is dedicated to developing, supporting, and sustaining the tourism sector across northern British Columbia, a region defined by its iconic The Great Wilderness and Infinite Coast. As one of six regional destination management organizations in the province, NBCTA operates as a non-profit association, stewarded by a board of directors elected by industry. The association collaborates strategically with the provincial government and Destination BC, a Provincial Crown Corporation, to advance the tourism sector throughout this distinctive region.NBCTA respectfully acknowledges the Lheidli T'enneh First Nation, on whose territory its main office operates. Furthermore, the association gratefully recognizes its work is conducted across the lands of Nations throughout the northern BC region. NBCTA honours its ongoing relationships with Indigenous Peoples and communities across northern BC, committing to continued collaborative efforts.

The 2026 Northern BC Tourism Summit brought tourism leaders, operators, and community partners together in Prince George from October 20–22 for three days of connection, collaboration, and learning.Northern BC Tourism Association opened the program with updates on regional initiatives supporting destination development, marketing, industry development, and the value of tourism in northern BC. Throughout the Summit, speakers and panelists explored industry resilience, Indigenous tourism, artificial intelligence, travel trade, destination storytelling, and place branding. Fifteen Tourism Industry Showcases also highlighted exciting projects, partnerships, and successes from across the region.Thank you to our speakers, sponsors, partners, and everyone who joined us to make this year's Summit a success.Browse the photo gallery to revisit memorable moments, reconnect with the highlights, and download your favourite photos.

NBCTA is a non-profit organization dedicated to promoting travel across one of Canada’s most vast and diverse regions, spanning from Mount Robson west to Haida Gwaii and north to the Yukon and Northwest Territories border. The association represents communities, businesses, and tourism operators throughout Northern BC, working collectively to build a strong and sustainable tourism economy. Guided by a passionate team and board of directors, NBCTA focuses on destination development, Indigenous tourism, sustainability, and responsible travel that respects both people and place.

NBCTA leads destination stewardship by working with stakeholders and communities to shape a sustainable future for tourism across northern BC. Through destination development strategies, the association fosters collaboration that strengthens infrastructure, supports workforce development, and enhances high-quality visitor experiences. In partnership with Indigenous Tourism BC, it advances Indigenous tourism as a vital cultural and economic force. With a strong commitment to sustainability, access, and inclusion, NBCTA ensures that tourism growth respects natural assets, honours cultural values, and benefits communities for generations to come.

NBCTA delivers programs that support businesses, communities, and stakeholders in building a resilient and thriving tourism sector. Through emergency preparedness initiatives, the association provides tools and resources to strengthen safety and communication during times of crisis. NBCTA also advocates for the value of tourism by equipping communities with resources to share its economic and cultural importance. Together, these programs foster collaboration, preparedness, and long-term success across northern BC.

Through content marketing, NBCTA creates and distributes inspiring stories across multiple channels, reaching qualified audiences in strategic markets. Its travel media program builds exposure by working with journalists and media outlets to share authentic stories of northern BC. Through travel trade, the association collaborates with international tour operators and travel agents to grow visitation. NBCTA also supports co-op marketing partnerships in the Northeast and Northwest, enabling communities to pool resources, amplify their impact, and showcase the unique experiences of northern BC.

Featured stories and updates from across northern BC. Here you’ll find articles on destination stewardship, marketing initiatives, and programs that highlight the work being done with communities, partners, and tourism operators across the region.

title: Guide to birdwatching in Estonia   Guide to birdwatching in Estonia
description: Hundreds of bird species call Estonia home, and large annual migrations make the country a prime destination for birdwatching in the Baltics.
headings: Where your morning alarm is a symphony of birdsong
Hundreds of species of birds call Estonia home, making it a top birdwatching destination in the Baltics.
Estonia has nearly 4,000 km of coastline, making it a perfect rest stop for migrating seabirds.
Nearly 400 bird species have been seen in Estonia, and more than 200 species nest here annually.
When spending a week watching birds in Estonia, you may see 180-190 different species.
When is the best time for a birdwatching holiday in Estonia?
The spring migration starts in March, culminates in May, and subsides by mid-June. September and October are good months to watch migratory birds gather, form flocks, and set off.
